rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for ordinary walking or moving along on foot.

example.english: Let's walk to the MTR station.
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 haang4 heoi3 dei6 tit3 zaam6 laa1

rows.note: Use this when the emphasis is on traveling on foot, especially over a distance or instead of using transport.

example.english: It takes twenty minutes to walk from here to the station.
example.traditional: 由呢度行路去車站要二十分鐘。
example.jyutping: jau4 ni1 dou6 haang4 lou6 heoi3 ce1 zaam6 jiu3 ji6 sap6 fan1 zung1

rows.note: This is the all-purpose noun for a walk taken for exercise or pleasure.

example.english: We go for a walk after dinner.
example.jyutping: ngo5 dei6 sik6 jyun4 faan6 heoi3 saan3 bou6

rows.note: Use this for a sidewalk or maintained route intended for pedestrians.

example.english: This sidewalk is wide enough for a comfortable walk.
example.traditional: 呢條行人路夠闊，行路好舒服。
example.jyutping: ni1 tiu4 hang4 jan4 lou6 gau3 fut3 haang4 lou6 hou2 syu1 fuk6

rows.note: Use this when “walk” refers to the length or distance of the journey rather than the outing itself.

example.english: The walk from home to the MTR station is not very far.
example.traditional: 由屋企行到地鐵站，路程唔算遠。
example.jyutping: jau4 uk1 kei2 haang4 dou3 dei6 tit3 zaam6 lou6 cing4 m4 syun3 jyun5

rows.note: Use this construction when taking a person or animal out for a walk, especially a dog.

example.english: I take my dog for a walk every day.
example.traditional: 我每日都帶隻狗去散步。
example.jyutping: ngo5 mui5 jat6 dou1 daai3 zek3 gau2 heoi3 saan3 bou6

rows.note: Use this for someone’s characteristic manner or style of walking.

example.english: Their walk is so distinctive that you can recognize them at once.
example.traditional: 佢行路姿勢好有型，一睇就知係佢。
example.jyutping: keoi5 haang4 lou6 zi1 sai3 hou2 jau5 jing4 jat1 tai2 zau6 zi1 hai6 keoi5
